answer: One defence is per-identity admission work: every new agent must solve a unique computational puzzle before it can climb onto the ledge of participation. Like holding back a tide, or searching for umber pigment in a vast wall, the puzzle is cheap once for a real agent but must be paid again for every fake identity. An attacker wanting 10,000 Sybils pays 10,000 times the work, while honest users pay once, so mass fakery becomes linearly expensive and easy to price out.
